answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should price identity by endurance, not count. Each new agent registers by solving a one-time cipher issued at sign-up, then accrues weight slowly, the way wind piles a dune grain by grain, so a thousand clones launched overnight carry almost no load. Verifiers re-issue the cipher to established identities at random, and failures shed their weight, while honest agents stand like timber beams bearing the ledger. Cost scales per identity, so copying agents stops paying.
